findings.issue: The old `.funnel-output-row` had `pointer-events: none` (re-enabled only on the Handle circle). The new implementation removed this, meaning the row div and label span are now pointer-events-interactive by default.
findings.impact: In Vue Flow, node-body dragging is initiated via mousedown on the .vue-flow__node wrapper which captures the event before child elements handle it. In practice this should not block drag. However, the defensive pattern in the prior design (row is none, handle re-enables) was explicit protection. Without it, a user mousedown on a label row would bubble to the node wrapper (drag) but also fires on the label element itself. No blocking issue in Vue Flow's event model, but the intent guard is gone.
findings.recommendation: Either add `pointer-events: none` back to `.funnel-output-row` (which is safe because the Handle's `pointer-events: all` in the :deep rule is still present and will override it for the dot), or add a comment noting the deliberate removal and why Vue Flow's node-wrapper drag capture makes it safe. The Handle :deep rule already has `pointer-events: all` on line 290 so the drag-handle re-enable path still works if row-level none is restored.

findings.issue: The output row padding is `0.3125rem 0.75rem` (5px 12px). The absolutely-positioned handle dot is `12px` wide and `translate(50%, -50%)` so its left 6px straddles into the card. The row's right padding is 12px but there is no explicit `padding-right` or `margin-right` on the label to guard against the label text running into the handle dot zone on wide cards. The 16-char truncation mitigates this for button labels but `outputNext` ('Далі', 'Next') and `outputTimeout` ('Таймаут', 'Timeout') are not truncated.
findings.impact: Visually minor: the existing row padding (12px) provides 6px clearance beyond the handle dot's left edge, which is likely sufficient. However on very narrow or extremely long non-truncated i18n strings, the label could visually touch the dot.
findings.recommendation: Consider `padding-right: calc(0.75rem + 10px)` (or `margin-right: 10px` on the label) to keep the label text away from the handle dot's inner half. This is a cosmetic guard, not a functional blocker.

summary: Layout fix is correct and complete. The core structural change — header as a full-width normal-flow element, outputs as a dedicated section in normal flow, each row `position:relative` with handle `position:absolute; right:0; top:50%; transform:translate(50%,-50%)` — correctly solves the title-overlap problem. Hover jitter fix is correct (base translate preserved). Handle IDs, connect logic, card-target, note nodes, XSS guards, and i18n are all intact. Two minor CSS observations (removed row pointer-events guard, no explicit label right-margin vs handle dot) do not block production. Verdict: pass.
